approach: In the wedge's accelerating frame the block is held by gravity, a leftward pseudo-force, the normal force and friction; resolve along the slope to isolate friction directly.

steps.text: Since the block does not slide relative to the incline, it shares the wedge's acceleration exactly.
steps.equation: a(block) = a(wedge) = 3 m/s², horizontal, to the right

steps.text: Work in the wedge's own frame, where the block is at rest under an added pseudo-force equal to its mass times the wedge's acceleration, directed opposite to that acceleration.
steps.equation: pseudo-force = m × 3 = 3m N, directed left, opposite the rightward acceleration

steps.text: Resolve gravity and the pseudo-force along the slope, which rises to the left at 37° to the horizontal, taking up-slope as positive.
steps.equation: gravity along slope = −m g sin37° = −6m N (down-slope); pseudo-force along slope = +m × 3 × cos37° = +2.4m N (up-slope)

steps.text: For the block to stay at rest in this frame, friction must balance the sum of these two along-slope components.
steps.equation: f = m g sin37° − m × 3 × cos37° = 6m − 2.4m = 3.6m N, directed up the slope

final_answer.value: f = 3.6m N, directed up the incline, where m is the block's mass in kg (equivalently f = 0.36mg).

common_mistakes.text: Ignoring that the incline itself is accelerating and treating it like a stationary incline gives friction as only the gravity component along the slope, m g sin37° = 6m N, instead of 3.6m N.
Adding the pseudo-force's along-slope component to gravity's instead of subtracting it gives m g sin37° + m × 3 × cos37° = 8.4m N instead of the correct 3.6m N.
